steps.description: If aggrieved by the decision: appeal from SAR to Judge in Chambers under Order 56 (Notice of Appeal Form 110, within 14 days of decision). Appeal from Judge in Chambers to Court of Appeal — file Notice of Appeal in High Court Registry within 30 days of sealed order. Confirm whether leave is required under s.68 Courts of Judicature Act 1964 (turn on Asia Commercial Finance order test).
steps.legalBasis: Order 56 ROC 2012; Courts of Judicature Act 1964, ss. 67–68; Rules of the Court of Appeal 1994
documents: Record of Appeal (if to Court of Appeal)

workflows.title: Interim Injunction (Prohibitory or Mandatory) — Inter Partes
workflows.description: Procedure to obtain an interim prohibitory or mandatory injunction inter partes pending trial, applying the American Cyanamid / Keet Gerald principles. For ex parte / freezing-asset injunctions see the Mareva workflow.
workflows.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 29; Specific Relief Act 1950, ss. 50–55; Courts of Judicature Act 1964, s. 25(2) and Schedule
workflows.applicableTo: Any party requiring interim restraint or compulsion against another party pending final disposal of the action (e.g., restraining breach of restrictive covenant, contractual undertaking, IP infringement, nuisance, trespass)
workflows.estimatedDuration: 2–6 weeks from filing to inter partes hearing decision

steps.title: Verify the Three-Limb Test (Keet Gerald / American Cyanamid)
steps.description: Confirm before filing: (a) there is a serious question to be tried; (b) damages would not be an adequate remedy for the applicant; (c) balance of convenience favours the grant. For mandatory injunctions, apply the higher Films Rover threshold — high degree of assurance the injunction will be vindicated at trial.
steps.legalBasis: American Cyanamid Co v Ethicon Ltd [1975] AC 396; Keet Gerald Francis Noel John v Mohd Noor [1995] 1 MLJ 193 (CA)

steps.title: Commence Substantive Action
steps.description: An interim injunction is parasitic on a substantive cause of action. File the Writ and Statement of Claim (or Originating Summons in suitable cases) before or simultaneously with the injunction application.

steps.title: Prepare Notice of Application and Supporting Affidavit
steps.description: Draft Notice of Application seeking the specific interim restraint or mandatory order, expressly including the applicant's undertaking as to damages (Order 29 r 2A). Affidavit must establish each limb of the test with supporting exhibits.

steps.title: File and Serve
steps.description: File Notice of Application in chambers, pay filing fee. Serve sealed copies on respondent at least 2 clear days before the hearing date. For genuine urgency, may seek abridgment of time or proceed ex parte (with full and frank disclosure).
steps.timeframe: Same day filing; 2+ clear days for service

steps.title: Inter Partes Hearing
steps.description: Both parties appear before Judge in Chambers. Applicant submits on each limb of the Keet Gerald test. Respondent argues against (no serious question; damages adequate; balance against). Court may grant, refuse, or grant on terms (e.g., cross-undertakings, fortified undertaking, security).

steps.title: Draft and Seal Order with Penal Notice
steps.description: If granted, draft the order setting out: (a) the precise restraint/mandate; (b) the express undertaking as to damages; (c) the duration (typically 'until trial or further order'); (d) costs. Endorse a Penal Notice ('If you, [Name], disobey this Order, you will be liable to be committed to prison for contempt of court'). Lodge for sealing.

steps.title: Personal Service of Sealed Order on Respondent
steps.description: The sealed order endorsed with penal notice MUST be served personally on the respondent (and any person to be bound, e.g., a director of a corporate respondent). Without proof of personal service, no contempt proceedings can be founded on breach.

steps.title: Monitor Compliance / Enforce by Committal
steps.description: If respondent breaches the injunction, apply for committal for contempt under Order 52 (leave application supported by affidavit; then committal motion). Penalty: imprisonment, fine, or sequestration of assets.

sampleDocuments: Affidavit in Support (with undertaking as to damages)
Draft Injunction Order with Penal Notice

workflows.title: Anton Piller (Search) Order — Ex Parte Application & Execution
workflows.description: Procedure to obtain and execute an Anton Piller order (search order) ex parte to enter the respondent's premises and preserve evidence under threat of destruction. Use sparingly — the three Ormrod conditions are stringent and abuse attracts indemnity costs and substantial damages.
workflows.legalBasis: Anton Piller KG v Manufacturing Processes Ltd [1976] Ch 55; Lian Keow Sdn Bhd v Paramjothy [1982] 1 MLJ 217 (FC); Courts of Judicature Act 1964, s. 25(2) & Schedule; Rules of Court 2012, Order 29 r 2
workflows.applicableTo: IP infringement, trade secrets, confidentiality breach, fraud — where there is clear evidence the respondent has incriminating items at risk of destruction
workflows.estimatedDuration: 1–3 days for ex parte order; execution same day; 2–4 weeks for inter partes return

steps.title: Verify the Three Ormrod Conditions
steps.description: Confirm: (a) extremely strong prima facie case; (b) very serious actual or potential damage; (c) clear evidence the respondent has incriminating items in possession with real possibility of destruction. Marginal cases will be refused.
steps.legalBasis: Anton Piller KG v Manufacturing Processes Ltd [1976] Ch 55; Lian Keow v Paramjothy [1982] 1 MLJ 217 (FC)
documents: Evidence of items in possession (e.g., emails, witness intel)

steps.title: Engage Independent Supervising Solicitor and Forensic Computer Expert
steps.description: Brief an independent supervising solicitor (not the applicant's regular firm) of standing and experience. Engage a forensic computer expert capable of hash-verified imaging. These engagements are mandatory safeguards.
steps.legalBasis: Universal Thermosensors Ltd v Hibben [1992] 1 WLR 840 (execution guidelines)
documents: Engagement letter to forensic IT expert

steps.title: Commence Substantive Action
steps.description: Anton Piller is parasitic on a substantive cause of action. File Writ + Statement of Claim simultaneously with the application.

steps.title: Prepare Ex Parte Notice of Application + Comprehensive Affidavit
steps.description: Affidavit must address every Ormrod condition and provide FULL AND FRANK DISCLOSURE — including matters adverse. Exhibit all evidence of risk of destruction. Include applicant's undertakings (damages; to issue proceedings; to abide by supervising solicitor; to compensate for damage).

steps.title: Ex Parte Hearing before Duty Judge
steps.description: Attend before Judge in Chambers (often duty judge). Address each Ormrod condition. Tender draft order incorporating standard safeguards (supervising solicitor; permitted hours; LPP carve-outs; right to consult solicitor).

steps.title: Execute the Search
steps.description: Search team (supervising solicitor, applicant's solicitor, forensic IT expert, applicant's representative) attends the premises during permitted hours (usually 9:30 a.m. start). Supervising solicitor reads and explains the order; allows respondent up to ~2 hours to obtain legal advice. Methodical room-by-room search; hash-verified forensic imaging; complete list and receipt of all items taken/imaged.
steps.legalBasis: Anton Piller order terms; Universal Thermosensors guidelines

steps.title: Lodge Originals with Court / Supervising Solicitor
steps.description: Within 24–48 hours, lodge originals seized with the court or supervising solicitor pending inspection. Forensic images held by IT expert under supervising solicitor's control.

steps.title: File Supervising Solicitor's Report
steps.description: Supervising solicitor files an independent report by affidavit on the conduct of the search — premises, persons present, items taken, any objections raised, any privilege segregations. This is the principal evidence on conduct of execution.
steps.legalBasis: Anton Piller order terms; Universal Thermosensors

steps.title: Inter Partes Return Hearing
steps.description: Both parties attend within 14 days. Respondent may seek discharge or variation. Court reviews compliance with conditions and execution conduct. Order may be continued, varied, or discharged with costs.

steps.title: Inspection of Materials and Privilege Review
steps.description: Court directs inspection regime. LPP and self-incrimination claims segregated and ruled on. Items not relevant to action returned. Forensic images limited to relevant material extracted; balance destroyed.

sampleDocuments: Ex Parte Notice of Application (Anton Piller)
Draft Anton Piller Order with Penal Notice

workflows.title: Striking Out Application — Order 18 r 19 ROC 2012
workflows.description: Procedure to strike out the whole or part of a pleading on grounds of (a) no reasonable cause of action/defence; (b) scandalous, frivolous or vexatious; (c) prejudice to fair trial; or (d) abuse of process.
workflows.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 18 r 19; Order 92 r 4 (inherent jurisdiction)
workflows.applicableTo: Defendants seeking to strike out a Statement of Claim; plaintiffs seeking to strike out a Defence; any party for limited paragraphs

steps.title: Identify the Limb(s) Relied Upon
steps.description: Determine whether the application is based on limb (a) (no reasonable cause/defence — pleading-only, no evidence), or limbs (b)–(d) (evidence permitted). Different procedural rules apply: limb (a) does not permit affidavit evidence (Order 18 r 19(2)).

steps.title: Draft Notice of Application + Affidavit (if applicable)
steps.description: Draft Notice of Application identifying the limb(s) and the precise paragraphs/pleading sought to be struck out. For limbs (b)–(d), prepare an affidavit exhibiting evidence (e.g., prior inconsistent pleading, evidence of abuse, third-party prior judgment for res judicata).

steps.title: File and Serve
steps.description: File at registry; pay filing fee (typically RM50). Serve on all parties at least 4 clear days before hearing.
steps.timeframe: Same day filing; 4+ days for service

steps.title: Receive Affidavit in Reply (if filed)
steps.description: Respondent typically opposes by affidavit (for limbs b–d) or argument only (limb a). Review carefully and consider rejoinder.

steps.title: Prepare Bundle of Authorities
steps.description: Key cases: Bandar Builder v UMBC [1993] 3 MLJ 36 (threshold); Tractors Malaysia v Tio Chee Hing [1975] 2 MLJ 1 (no reasonable cause); Henderson v Henderson (abuse). Mark passages.

steps.title: Chambers Hearing
steps.description: Attend before Judge in Chambers or SAR. Argue strict 'plain and obvious' threshold for limb (a); evidential basis for limbs (b)–(d). Address opponent's arguable points.

steps.title: Order and Consequences
steps.description: If granted in whole — action dismissed; consider whether judgment can be entered. If granted in part — pleading amended; case proceeds. If refused — costs typically against applicant; consider appeal.

sampleDocuments: Notice of Application — Striking Out (Order 18 r 19)
Bundle of Authorities (Bandar Builder, Tractors Malaysia)

workflows.title: Specific Discovery Application — Order 24 r 7 ROC 2012
workflows.description: Procedure for specific discovery of documents under Order 24 r 7 where general discovery is incomplete or where particular documents (or classes of documents) are believed to be in the respondent's possession, custody or power and are relevant to the action.
workflows.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 24 r 7; Compagnie Financiere v Peruvian Guano (1882) 11 QBD 55
workflows.applicableTo: Any party requiring discovery of specific documents not produced under general discovery, or pre-action / against non-parties under Order 24 r 7A

steps.title: Identify Documents with Particularity
steps.description: List specific documents or narrow classes (e.g., 'all emails between X and Y between [date] and [date] concerning [project]'). Vague applications fail. Confirm relevance via Peruvian Guano test.
documents: Internal review of pleadings and General Discovery list

steps.title: Establish Possession, Custody or Power
steps.description: Affidavit must depose to grounds for belief that the respondent has the documents (correspondence, witness intel, business practice). Mere speculation is insufficient.
documents: Evidence of existence (e.g., references in other documents)

steps.title: Draft Notice of Application + Affidavit
steps.description: Notice of Application sets out the categories of documents sought. Affidavit deposes to relevance, existence, possession/custody/power, and that the respondent has not produced them.

steps.title: File and Serve
steps.description: Standard filing; service at least 4 clear days before hearing.

steps.title: Affidavit in Reply
steps.description: Respondent typically claims (a) documents do not exist; (b) not in possession; (c) privilege; (d) irrelevance; (e) oppression. Address these in rejoinder.

steps.title: Hearing and Order
steps.description: Court may order: (a) production within stated time; (b) inspection; (c) further affidavit on grounds of any privilege claim; (d) refusal. Consequences of non-compliance: striking out, contempt, or adverse inferences at trial.
steps.timeframe: Hearing day; production typically 14–28 days after order

sampleDocuments: Notice of Application — Specific Discovery (Order 24 r 7)

workflows.title: Security for Costs Application — Order 23 ROC 2012
workflows.description: Procedure for a defendant to obtain an order requiring the plaintiff to provide security for the defendant's likely costs of defending the action — typically against foreign plaintiffs, nominal plaintiffs, or impecunious corporate plaintiffs (s.351 Companies Act 2016).
workflows.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 23; Companies Act 2016, s.351
workflows.applicableTo: Defendants in civil actions where plaintiff is foreign / nominal / impecunious corporate / has misstated address / has changed address to evade litigation consequences
workflows.estimatedDuration: 4–8 weeks from filing to disposal; further time for security to be furnished

steps.title: Establish Ground for Security
steps.description: Confirm one or more grounds: (a) plaintiff resident outside Malaysia; (b) nominal plaintiff; (c) misstated address; (d) evasive address change; or (e) corporate plaintiff with credible evidence of inability to pay defendant's costs (s.351 CA 2016).
steps.legalBasis: Order 23 r 1 ROC 2012; Companies Act 2016 s.351
documents: Evidence of foreign residence; financial statements; investigations

steps.title: Compute Quantum of Likely Costs
steps.description: Estimate party-party costs to a particular stage (close of pleadings, discovery, trial). Typically claim 50–80% of estimated costs as security. Itemise: court fees, counsel fees, solicitor fees, expert fees.
steps.legalBasis: Order 59 ROC 2012; Bill of Costs scales

steps.title: Draft Notice of Application + Affidavit
steps.description: Affidavit deposes to the ground, the financial position of plaintiff, the cost estimate, and the prejudice if no security ordered. For corporate plaintiff: exhibit credible evidence of financial weakness (e.g., audited accounts, news reports, judgments).

steps.title: File and Serve
steps.description: Standard filing; serve at least 4 clear days before hearing.

steps.title: Hearing
steps.description: Court considers grounds, merits of plaintiff's claim, plaintiff's resources, and whether order would stifle a genuine claim. Discretionary balance.
steps.legalBasis: Order 23 r 1(1); KP Singh v Bahadur Singh principles

steps.title: Order — Form of Security
steps.description: If granted: order specifies amount, form (cash deposit into court, bank guarantee from licensed bank, solicitor's undertaking), and time for furnishing (typically 21–28 days). Failure to furnish = stay of proceedings until furnished, or eventual striking out.

sampleDocuments: Notice of Application — Security for Costs (Order 23)
Affidavit in Support (with costs estimate and financial evidence)

workflows.title: Setting Aside Default Judgment — Order 13 r 8 / Order 19 r 9 ROC 2012
workflows.description: Procedure for a defendant to set aside a default judgment entered against them for failure to enter appearance (Order 13) or failure to file defence (Order 19). Distinguishes between regular (procedural irregularity) and irregular (substantive defence) categories.
workflows.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 13 r 8; Order 19 r 9; Evans v Bartlam [1937] AC 473; Mageswari v United Asian Bank [1985] 1 MLJ 145
workflows.applicableTo: Defendants against whom a default judgment has been entered, seeking to set it aside and defend the action on the merits

steps.title: Investigate the Default
steps.description: Determine: (a) was service proper? (procedural irregularity → set aside as of right); (b) was there reasonable cause for failure to appear/defend?; (c) is there a defence on the merits?

steps.title: Draft Notice of Application + Affidavit + Draft Defence
steps.description: Affidavit deposes to: (a) circumstances of default; (b) reasonable explanation; (c) defence on the merits; (d) promptness in applying. Annex Draft Defence showing triable issues. (For irregularly entered judgments, focus on the procedural irregularity.)

steps.title: File, Serve, and Apply for Stay of Execution
steps.description: Filing fee. Serve on plaintiff. Consider simultaneous application to stay execution of the judgment (Order 55 r 16) so enforcement does not proceed pending the application.

steps.title: Hearing
steps.description: Plaintiff often opposes. Court applies Evans v Bartlam test: defence on merits + reasonable explanation + promptness. For procedural irregularity: set aside as of right.
steps.legalBasis: Order 13 r 8; Order 19 r 9; Evans v Bartlam

steps.title: Order — Often on Conditions
steps.description: If set aside: typically on terms — payment into court, costs to plaintiff in cause, expedited timetable. Defence to be filed within stated time. Action proceeds.

sampleDocuments: Notice of Application — Setting Aside Default Judgment
Affidavit in Support (reason + defence on merits + promptness)
Application for Stay of Execution (if needed)

workflows.title: Recovery of Loan — Writ Action
workflows.description: End-to-end procedure for a bank to recover an outstanding loan through a full writ action in the High Court, from pre-action correspondence to trial and enforcement.
workflows.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012; Limitation Act 1953; Contracts Act 1950
workflows.applicableTo: Banks and financial institutions recovering unsecured or partially secured loan debts

steps.title: Pre-Action Steps and Demand Letter
steps.description: Issue a formal letter of demand to the borrower specifying the outstanding amount (principal, interest, charges), and demanding payment within 14 days.
steps.legalBasis: Contract general principles; BNM guidelines on debt collection

steps.title: Check Limitation Period
steps.description: Confirm that the action is not statute-barred. For breach of loan agreement: 6 years from date of breach. If guarantee: 6 years from date of demand on guarantor.

steps.title: File Writ and Statement of Claim
steps.description: File Writ of Summons and Statement of Claim. The SOC must particularize the agreement, breach, and quantum claimed.

steps.title: Attempt Summary Judgment
steps.description: After defendant enters appearance, file Order 14 application for summary judgment. If no arguable defence, obtain judgment without trial.

steps.title: Case Management
steps.description: If summary judgment fails, attend Case Management Conference before the Senior Assistant Registrar. Comply with directions on pleadings, discovery, and witness statements.

steps.title: Trial
steps.description: Attend trial. Bank calls witnesses (relationship manager, credit officer) to prove the loan and default. Defendant cross-examines. Plaintiff must prove on balance of probabilities.

steps.title: Judgment and Enforcement
steps.description: Obtain judgment. If defendant does not pay, enforce by WSS, garnishee, charging order, or bankruptcy/winding up.

workflows.title: Hire Purchase Repossession and Deficiency Claim
workflows.description: Step-by-step procedure for a bank to repossess a hire purchase vehicle after default and subsequently recover any deficiency from the hirer.
workflows.legalBasis: Hire-Purchase Act 1967 (Act 212); Rules of Court 2012
workflows.applicableTo: Banks and finance companies providing hire purchase financing
workflows.estimatedDuration: 3-9 months from default to deficiency judgment

steps.title: Verify Default and One-Third Rule
steps.description: Confirm the hirer has defaulted. Calculate whether the hirer has paid one-third or more of the hire purchase price. If yes, court order required before repossession (s. 16 HPA 1967).

steps.title: Serve Notice of Default (Second Schedule)
steps.description: Serve a written notice in the Second Schedule format specifying the amount overdue and giving the hirer 21 days to pay before repossession.

steps.title: Repossession of Vehicle (If Less Than One-Third Paid)
steps.description: If less than one-third paid, repossess the vehicle after expiry of notice. Use repossession agents if necessary. Do not breach the peace.

steps.title: Obtain Court Order for Repossession (If One-Third or More Paid)
steps.description: File an application in court (Originating Summons) for an order of repossession. Court will consider whether to grant, refuse, or give the hirer time to pay.

steps.title: Serve Third Schedule Notice After Repossession
steps.description: Within 7 days of repossession, serve a notice (Third Schedule format) on the hirer informing them of the repossession and their right to redeem within 21 days.

steps.title: Sale of Repossessed Vehicle
steps.description: If hirer does not redeem within 21 days, sell the vehicle by public auction. Must obtain the best price reasonably obtainable. Notify hirer of sale in advance.

steps.title: Deficiency Claim in Court
steps.description: If sale proceeds are less than the outstanding balance, the owner may sue for the deficiency. File a Writ of Summons for the shortfall amount.

workflows.title: Appointment of Receiver and Manager
workflows.description: Procedure for a bank to appoint a Receiver and Manager over a company's assets pursuant to a debenture, outside of court proceedings.
workflows.legalBasis: Companies Act 2016 (Act 777), Part IV Division 8; Debenture Agreement
workflows.applicableTo: Banks holding a debenture (fixed and floating charge) over company assets

steps.title: Confirm Crystallisation Event
steps.description: Verify that a crystallisation event has occurred under the debenture — typically: default in payment, breach of covenant, winding up petition, material adverse change, or enforcement clause.

steps.title: Identify and Instruct Receiver
steps.description: Select a licensed insolvency practitioner (Licensed Receiver under s. 441 CA 2016) to act as Receiver and Manager. Ensure no conflict of interest.

steps.title: Execute Deed of Appointment
steps.description: Execute the Deed of Appointment of Receiver and Manager, signed by authorised officers of the bank. The appointment takes effect on execution.
documents: Deed of Appointment of Receiver and Manager

steps.title: Notify Company and Relevant Parties
steps.description: Serve notice of appointment on the company's registered office. Receiver publishes notice to company officers, creditors, and customers.

steps.title: File Documents with CCM
steps.description: The Receiver files Form 64A (Notice of Appointment) and Form 64B (Receiver's Statement of Affairs) with the Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM).

steps.title: Realisation of Assets
steps.description: The Receiver manages the business and realises assets to pay the chargee (bank). Receiver has broad powers to sell assets, collect debts, and carry on business.

sampleDocuments: Deed of Appointment of Receiver and Manager

workflows.title: Mediation and Alternative Dispute Resolution in Banking
workflows.description: The process of resolving banking disputes through the Financial Services Ombudsman Scheme (FSOS) and court-annexed mediation under the Mediation Act 2012.
workflows.legalBasis: Mediation Act 2012 (Act 749); Financial Services Ombudsman Scheme (FSOS) under FSA 2013
workflows.applicableTo: Consumer banking disputes and commercial banking disputes

steps.title: Internal Bank Complaint Process
steps.description: File a formal complaint with the bank's internal complaints unit. Bank must respond within 14 business days (consumer) or 20 business days (commercial) under BNM's Guideline on Complaints Handling.
steps.legalBasis: BNM Guidelines on Complaints Handling; FSA 2013

steps.title: FSOS Complaint (Consumer Disputes)
steps.description: If unsatisfied with bank's response, consumer may lodge a complaint with the Ombudsman for Financial Services (OFS). Maximum eligible amount: RM250,000 for financial loss. Free for consumers.
steps.legalBasis: Financial Services Ombudsman Scheme Rules; FSA 2013 s. 127

steps.title: Refer to Kuala Lumpur Mediation Centre
steps.description: For commercial disputes or where FSOS does not apply, parties may agree to mediate at the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) or Kuala Lumpur Mediation Centre.

steps.title: Court-Annexed Mediation
steps.description: If court proceedings are commenced, the court may order mandatory mediation. Parties attend a mediation session with an accredited mediator. Any settlement is recorded as a consent order.

workflows.title: Breach of Contract — Writ Action
workflows.description: Step-by-step procedure for commencing and conducting a breach of contract claim by Writ of Summons in the Malaysian High Court or Sessions Court, from letter of demand to judgment and enforcement.
workflows.legalBasis: Contracts Act 1950; Rules of Court 2012, Orders 6, 18, 25, 34; Limitation Act 1953
workflows.applicableTo: All contractual disputes — sale of goods, services, commercial agreements, professional retainers

steps.title: Pre-Litigation: Letter of Demand
steps.description: Solicitors send a formal letter of demand to the defaulting party specifying the amount claimed, basis of the claim, and a deadline (usually 14 days) for payment or remedy. This is not mandatory but is strongly advised as it demonstrates good faith and may lead to settlement.
documents: Evidence of breach (correspondence, delivery records, etc.)

steps.title: Filing the Writ of Summons
steps.description: If no satisfactory response, file a Writ of Summons (Form 1 ROC 2012) in the High Court (claim above RM250,000) or Sessions Court (RM50,000-RM250,000). The Writ must identify the plaintiff and defendant, state the general nature of the claim, and be signed by the plaintiff's solicitor.
steps.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 6; Courts of Judicature Act 1964; Subordinate Courts Act 1948
documents: Statement of Claim (usually endorsed on the Writ)

steps.title: Service of Writ on Defendant
steps.description: Serve the sealed Writ on the defendant by personal service (ideal) or, if unavailable, by substituted service (registered post + advertisement) with court leave. Defendant has 12 days (within Malaysia) or extended time if overseas to enter appearance.
documents: Original sealed Writ + copies for service

steps.title: Default Judgment (if no appearance)
steps.description: If defendant fails to enter appearance within the prescribed time, plaintiff may apply for Judgment in Default of Appearance under Order 13 ROC 2012 without a trial. For liquidated claims, judgment is granted as of right. For unliquidated claims, damages must be assessed.
documents: Request for Entry of Default Judgment

steps.title: Pleadings: Statement of Claim and Defence
steps.description: If defendant enters appearance, plaintiff serves Statement of Claim (if not already endorsed on Writ). Defendant has 14 days to file and serve Defence. Plaintiff may file Reply if necessary. Pleadings establish the material facts in issue.

steps.title: Interlocutory Applications (if any)
steps.description: Either party may apply for interlocutory orders: summary judgment under Order 14 (where defendant has no arguable defence), striking out under Order 18 r.19, security for costs, or interim injunctions under Order 29.

steps.title: Discovery and Inspection
steps.description: Standard discovery under Order 24 ROC 2012: both parties exchange lists of documents relevant to issues in the pleadings. Documents are inspected and copies taken. Specific discovery may be ordered for specific categories of documents. E-discovery increasingly important in commercial disputes.

steps.title: Pre-Trial Case Management
steps.description: Case Management Conference before the Judge/Senior AR: parties agree on issues, witnesses, agreed bundles, and trial dates. Court may order mediation at this stage. Trial dates fixed.

steps.title: Trial
steps.description: Trial conducted in open court. Plaintiff's witnesses (oral evidence-in-chief, cross-examination, re-examination). Defendant's witnesses. Closing submissions. Judge reserves judgment.

steps.title: Enforcement of Judgment
steps.description: Upon obtaining judgment, enforce by: (a) Writ of Seizure and Sale (O.45) against movable/immovable property; (b) Garnishee proceedings (O.49) against money owed by third parties to the defendant; (c) Charging Order (O.50) on defendant's shares/partnership interests; (d) Bankruptcy (if individual) or Winding Up (if company) as last resort.
steps.legalBasis: ROC 2012, Orders 45, 49, 50; Insolvency Act 1967; Companies Act 2016
documents: Writ of Seizure and Sale / Garnishee Notice / Charging Order Summons

workflows.title: Motor Vehicle Accident — Negligence Claim
workflows.description: Procedure for pursuing a civil claim for personal injury and property damage arising from a motor vehicle accident (MVA) in Malaysia, from police report to judgment or settlement.
workflows.legalBasis: Civil Law Act 1956; Motor Vehicles (Third Party Risks and Compensation) Act 1987; Rules of Court 2012
workflows.applicableTo: Road traffic accidents involving personal injury and/or property damage

steps.title: Police Report and Medical Treatment
steps.description: File a police report within 24 hours of the accident. Obtain immediate medical treatment and keep all medical receipts. The police report is crucial evidence. The traffic police will conduct an investigation and may issue a summons to the at-fault party.
documents: Photographs of accident scene and damage

steps.title: Insurance Notification and Claim
steps.description: Notify your own insurer (in case of own damage) and the at-fault party's insurer. The third-party insurer (of the at-fault driver) is directly liable for personal injury and death claims — s.96 Road Transport Act 1987. Lodge third-party claim with the insurer.
steps.legalBasis: Motor Vehicles (Third Party Risks and Compensation) Act 1987, s.96; Road Transport Act 1987

steps.title: Letter of Demand
steps.description: Solicitors send a formal letter of demand to the at-fault party and their insurer claiming: (a) medical expenses, (b) loss of earnings, (c) general damages (pain and suffering, loss of amenities), (d) vehicle repair/replacement, (e) transport costs.
steps.timeframe: 2-6 months after accident (after medical treatment completed)

steps.title: Filing Suit
steps.description: If insurer rejects claim or offers inadequate settlement, file a Writ of Summons naming the at-fault driver and/or the registered owner as defendants. Issue is normally against the driver and the insurer is joined under s.96 MTAR 1987. For property damage only, Magistrate's Court may have jurisdiction (claims up to RM100,000).
steps.legalBasis: ROC 2012, Order 6; Civil Law Act 1956; MTAR 1987
documents: Statement of Claim (detailing all heads of damage)
steps.timeframe: Within 6 years of accident (Limitation Act 1953, s.6(1)); only 36 months where a public authority is the defendant (Public Authorities Protection Act 1948)

steps.title: Medical Assessment and Expert Evidence
steps.description: Plaintiff should obtain a medico-legal report from a medical specialist. Defendant may require the plaintiff to attend an examination by their own medical expert. Reports are exchanged. Court will assess damages based on medical evidence.

steps.title: Assessment of Damages — Heads of Claim
steps.description: Special Damages (precisely calculable): medical expenses (all receipts), loss of earnings (payslips, employer's letter), transport costs, vehicle repair. General Damages (assessed by court): pain and suffering, loss of amenities of life, loss of future earnings/capacity, future medical care. Reference to personal injury award guidelines — Judicial Guidelines for Personal Injuries Awards published by Malaysian courts.
steps.legalBasis: Civil Law Act 1956, s.28A (post-1984 amendments for personal injury); Judicial Guidelines for Award of Damages

steps.title: Settlement Negotiations
steps.description: Most MVA cases settle before trial. Insurer will make an offer after reviewing medical reports. Consider: the quantum of damages claimed vs. offered, contributory negligence (if plaintiff was partly at fault, damages are reduced proportionately), and litigation costs. Mediation increasingly used.
steps.legalBasis: Civil Law Act 1956, s.12 (contributory negligence); Order 34A ROC 2012 (mediation)

steps.title: Judgment and Satisfaction
steps.description: If no settlement, trial proceeds. Court determines: liability (Was the defendant negligent? Was plaintiff contributorily negligent?), and quantum (amount of damages). Judgment entered. Enforcement against insurer under s.96 MTAR 1987.

workflows.title: Unfair Dismissal — Industrial Court Proceedings
workflows.description: The complete procedure for an employee to challenge an unfair or wrongful dismissal before the Industrial Relations Department and the Industrial Court in Malaysia, from complaint through award.
workflows.legalBasis: Industrial Relations Act 1967 (Act 177), ss.20-30; Industrial Court Rules 1976
workflows.applicableTo: All employees covered by the IRA 1967 — no wage ceiling for dismissal claims

steps.title: Filing Complaint with Director General of Industrial Relations (DGIR)
steps.description: Within 60 DAYS of dismissal, the employee must file a written complaint (Form A — Representation) with the nearest Industrial Relations Department office. This 60-day limit is jurisdictional — strictly enforced. Include: name and address of employer, date of dismissal, grounds for complaint, and relief sought (reinstatement or compensation).

steps.title: Conciliation by Director General
steps.description: The DGIR invites both parties to a conciliation meeting. The officer facilitates negotiation without deciding on the merits. If settlement reached, a consent award is recorded. If no settlement, the DGIR refers the matter to the Industrial Court for hearing. Average conciliation period: 1-3 months.
documents: DGIR referral letter to Industrial Court (if not settled)

steps.title: Industrial Court — Case Management
steps.description: Upon referral, the Industrial Court issues a Notice of Hearing. Parties file written statements of case: (a) Claimant's Statement; (b) Employer's Response. Exchange of documents. The court may order further and better particulars.
documents: List of documents to be relied upon

steps.title: Domestic Inquiry Records Review
steps.description: The Court will scrutinise the domestic inquiry (DI) proceedings — the foundation of the employer's case. Was the DI conducted fairly? Was the charge specific? Was the claimant given sufficient notice? Was an impartial panel convened? Fundamental breaches of natural justice in DI weaken the employer's case significantly.
steps.legalBasis: Natural justice principles; Dreamland Corporation (M) Sdn Bhd v Choong Chin Sooi [1988] 1 MLJ 111

steps.title: Full Hearing — Evidence
steps.description: Hearing before an Industrial Court Chairman. Employer bears the burden of proving just cause and excuse. Employer's witnesses first (misconduct cases); claimant's witnesses respond. Evidence given orally on oath. Rules of evidence are relaxed — industrial court has wide discretion.
steps.legalBasis: Industrial Relations Act 1967, s.30; Evidence Act 1950 (modified application)

steps.title: Written Submissions
steps.description: After evidence, both parties file written submissions addressing: (a) whether just cause and excuse was established, (b) relevant Industrial Court awards as precedents, (c) quantum of back wages and compensation if dismissal was without just cause.

steps.title: Industrial Court Award
steps.description: The Court issues a written Award. If dismissal was without just cause: (a) Reinstatement with back wages (up to 24 months in practice), or (b) Compensation in lieu (24 months' wages maximum in most cases). If dismissal was justified: complaint dismissed. Award is binding on parties.

steps.title: Judicial Review of Award (if necessary)
steps.description: If either party is dissatisfied with the Award, they may apply for judicial review (O.53 ROC 2012) within 3 months of the Award. The High Court reviews on grounds of illegality, irrationality, or procedural impropriety — not on the merits of the dismissal.

workflows.title: Divorce Proceedings (Civil) — Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976
workflows.description: Procedure for dissolution of a non-Muslim civil marriage in Malaysia under the Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976, including ancillary matters (custody, maintenance, division of matrimonial assets).
workflows.legalBasis: Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976 (Act 164); Rules of Court 2012; Guardianship of Infants Act 1961
workflows.applicableTo: Non-Muslim married couples in Malaysia (civil or civil-registered marriages)

steps.title: Grounds Assessment and Initial Advice
steps.description: Assess whether the marriage has broken down irretrievably. Advise on grounds available — adultery, unreasonable behaviour, desertion (2 years), separation (2 or 5 years), or joint petition (mutual consent after 2 years of marriage). Confirm the parties' domicile or habitual residence in Malaysia (jurisdictional requirement).

steps.title: Filing Petition for Divorce
steps.description: File a Petition for Divorce (Form 8A) in the High Court Family Division or Sessions Court (where matrimonial assets are below RM250,000). Petition must state: parties' details, date and place of marriage, grounds for divorce, and relief sought (decree nisi, custody, maintenance, division of assets).
steps.legalBasis: LRA 1976, s.50; Divorce and Matrimonial Proceedings Rules 1980

steps.title: Service on Respondent
steps.description: Serve the Petition and supporting documents on the respondent personally. If respondent is overseas, apply for leave to serve outside jurisdiction. Respondent has 21 days after service to file Answer (if contesting) or Acknowledgement of Service (if not contesting).

steps.title: Ancillary Matters — Affidavit of Means
steps.description: Both parties must file an Affidavit of Means disclosing all assets, liabilities, income, and expenses. This is the basis for determining maintenance and division of matrimonial assets. Full and frank disclosure is a legal obligation — non-disclosure may lead to setting aside of orders.
steps.legalBasis: LRA 1976, ss.76-96; Divorce and Matrimonial Proceedings Rules 1980

steps.title: Hearing of Ancillary Matters — Custody
steps.description: If custody is contested, the court conducts a welfare inquiry. Each parent files an affidavit on: housing, employment, relationship with children, proposed childcare arrangements. Court may order a Social Welfare Report. Children above a certain age may express preference. Paramount principle: welfare of the child.
steps.legalBasis: LRA 1976, s.88; Guardianship of Infants Act 1961; s.88 LRA 1976

steps.title: Decree Nisi
steps.description: After hearing, court pronounces the Decree Nisi — a conditional order of divorce. The marriage is not yet dissolved. If contested, only after trial on the petition. If uncontested, on affidavit evidence and court is satisfied. Ancillary orders (custody, maintenance, asset division) are usually made at this stage or separately.
documents: Orders for custody, maintenance, division of assets

steps.title: Decree Absolute
steps.description: The Decree Nisi is made Absolute after 3 months from the date of the Decree Nisi (s.55 LRA 1976). Either party may apply for the Decree Absolute after this period. The marriage is finally dissolved on the date of the Decree Absolute. Parties are free to remarry.

steps.title: Enforcement of Orders
steps.description: Enforce maintenance orders by: garnishee order (against employer's salary payments), writ of seizure and sale, or committal for contempt. Enforce asset division orders by court order to effect transfer of property (if one party refuses, the Registrar may sign documents on that party's behalf under s.79 Specific Relief Act 1950).
steps.legalBasis: ROC 2012, Orders 45, 49, 52; Specific Relief Act 1950, s.79

workflows.title: Judicial Review Application — Order 53 ROC 2012
workflows.description: Procedure for applying for judicial review in the High Court to challenge a decision, act, or failure to act by a public authority in Malaysia, from leave application to substantive hearing and remedies.
workflows.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 53; Administrative Law (common law); Federal Constitution
workflows.applicableTo: Challenges to decisions of Government ministries, statutory authorities, local authorities, tribunals, and other public bodies

steps.title: Identify the Decision and Grounds
steps.description: Identify the specific decision, act, or omission to be challenged. Confirm: (a) the decision-maker is a public authority exercising a public function; (b) there is a cognisable ground of review (illegality, irrationality, procedural impropriety, legitimate expectation); (c) the 3-month time limit has not expired.
steps.legalBasis: ROC 2012, O.53 r.3(6); Federal Constitution, Art.4, 5, 8, 135
documents: Copy of the decision under challenge

steps.title: Prepare Ex Parte Application for Leave
steps.description: File ex parte Originating Summons supported by: (a) Statement (O.53 r.3(2)) — name, relief sought, grounds, material facts; (b) Affidavit in Support verifying facts and exhibiting all relevant documents. Application is filed in the High Court Judicial Review Division.
documents: Written submissions in support of leave

steps.title: Leave Hearing (Ex Parte)
steps.description: The judge hears the leave application in chambers — usually without the opposing party (ex parte). The test for leave: Is there a prima facie arguable case on any ground of review? If leave granted, the matter proceeds to substantive hearing. If leave refused, the applicant may appeal to the Court of Appeal.

steps.title: Notice to Respondent and Filing Substantive Affidavits
steps.description: Upon grant of leave, serve the OS and supporting documents on the respondent and all interested parties. Respondent files Affidavit in Opposition within the time directed by the court. Applicant may file Affidavit in Reply. All evidence in JR proceedings is by affidavit — oral evidence is rare.

steps.title: Written Submissions
steps.description: Both parties file comprehensive written submissions addressing: (a) the factual background; (b) applicable legal principles; (c) grounds of review argued; (d) relief sought and why it is appropriate. The JR hearing is heavily argument-based.

steps.title: Substantive Hearing
steps.description: Full hearing before the High Court Judge. Counsel make oral submissions elaborating on written arguments. The judge may ask questions. Witnesses are rarely called — proceedings are based on the affidavit evidence. The judge may reserve judgment.

steps.title: Remedies
steps.description: If successful: Court may issue — (a) Certiorari: quash the unlawful decision; (b) Mandamus: compel performance of a public duty; (c) Prohibition: prevent future unlawful action; (d) Declaration of the legal position; (e) Injunction (rare in JR against Government). Costs awarded to successful party.
steps.legalBasis: ROC 2012, O.53 r.2; Specific Relief Act 1950

steps.title: Appeal
steps.description: Either party may appeal to the Court of Appeal within 30 days of the High Court judgment (Courts of Judicature Act 1964, s.68). If the appeal involves a question of law of general public importance, a further appeal to the Federal Court is available (with leave).
steps.legalBasis: Courts of Judicature Act 1964, ss.67-68; ROC 2012, Order 55

workflows.title: Company Oppression Petition — Section 346 Companies Act 2016
workflows.description: Procedure for filing and conducting an oppression petition by a minority shareholder under s.346 of the Companies Act 2016 in the High Court (Company Division), seeking relief for commercially unfair conduct of the company's affairs.
workflows.legalBasis: Companies Act 2016 (Act 777), ss.346-347; Rules of Court 2012, Order 88
workflows.applicableTo: Minority shareholders of private and public companies in Malaysia

steps.title: Assess Oppression and Relief Sought
steps.description: Identify specific acts of oppression: exclusion from management, failure to pay dividends, diversion of company's business to a competing entity, improper use of company funds for personal benefit, failure to provide accounts. Assess relief: share buyout at fair value, conduct order, declaration, or winding up as last resort.

steps.title: File Originating Petition
steps.description: File an Originating Petition (OP) in the High Court (Company Division). The OP must set out: petitioner's shareholding, respondents (company + individual directors/majority shareholders), full facts of the oppressive conduct, and relief sought. Verified by the petitioner's affidavit.

steps.title: Interim Relief — Injunction to Preserve Assets
steps.description: If there is a risk of asset dissipation or further oppressive conduct pending the hearing, apply immediately for an interlocutory injunction restraining the respondents from: transferring company assets, incurring unusual liabilities, or removing the petitioner as director.
steps.timeframe: Urgently — as soon as OP is filed

steps.title: Respondent's Answer
steps.description: The company and individual respondents file an affidavit in answer denying oppression and justifying their conduct. Directors will defend: decisions were made bona fide for the benefit of the company; petitioner was excluded for legitimate business reasons; proper accounts were maintained.

steps.title: Discovery and Valuation
steps.description: The key practical issue: what is the fair value of the petitioner's shares if a buyout is ordered? Appoint independent valuer (accountant/business valuer). Extensive discovery of company's financial records. May require forensic accountant to uncover wrongful transactions.

steps.title: Full Hearing
steps.description: Trial of the petition. Evidence from petitioner's witnesses and respondents' witnesses. Court assesses whether the conduct was commercially unfair (not merely technically legal). Petitioner's expert valuer and respondents' expert valuer may both be called.
steps.legalBasis: Companies Act 2016, s.346; Re Kong Thai Sawmill (Miri) Sdn Bhd [1978] 2 MLJ 227

steps.title: Court Order
steps.description: If petition succeeds: Court orders share buyout at fair value determined by the valuer/court; or conduct order regulating future affairs; or declaration. If petition dismissed: petitioner bears costs. Court has wide discretion under s.346(2).

workflows.title: CIPAA Adjudication — Construction Payment Dispute
workflows.description: The statutory adjudication process under the Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012 (CIPAA 2012) for fast-track resolution of payment disputes in the Malaysian construction industry.
workflows.legalBasis: Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012 (Act 746); AIAC Adjudication Rules
workflows.applicableTo: Construction contracts and construction consultancy service contracts in Malaysia (excluding residential owner-occupier dwelling houses)

steps.title: Serve Payment Claim (s.5 CIPAA)
steps.description: The claimant (contractor, sub-contractor, consultant) serves a written Payment Claim on the respondent. The Payment Claim must: identify the construction contract, describe the work done or services rendered, state the claimed amount, and state the basis of the claim. No prescribed form — must be sufficiently clear.
steps.timeframe: When payment is due and unpaid

steps.title: Payment Response (s.6 CIPAA)
steps.description: Respondent must serve a Payment Response within 10 working days of the Payment Claim (for disputed amounts). The response must: state the response amount (agreed amount), and provide reasons for any disputed amount. Failure to respond is deemed admission of the full claimed amount.
steps.timeframe: Within 10 working days of Payment Claim

steps.title: Notice of Adjudication (s.8 CIPAA)
steps.description: If payment is disputed or unpaid, the claimant serves a Notice of Adjudication on the respondent initiating the adjudication process. The Notice must identify the contract, describe the dispute, state the relief sought, and propose an adjudicator (if any).
steps.timeframe: After expiry of Payment Response period

steps.title: Appointment of Adjudicator (s.9)
steps.description: Parties have 10 working days to agree on an adjudicator. If no agreement, either party may apply to the AIAC Director to appoint an adjudicator. The AIAC will appoint from its panel within 5 working days. Adjudicator must disclose any conflicts of interest.
documents: Joint nomination of adjudicator / AIAC appointment request

steps.title: Adjudication Claim (s.10)
steps.description: Claimant files the Adjudication Claim within 10 working days of the adjudicator's acceptance. Must include: all facts, documents, and legal arguments supporting the claim. Submit concurrently to the adjudicator and serve on the respondent.
steps.timeframe: Within 10 working days of adjudicator's acceptance

steps.title: Adjudication Response (s.11)
steps.description: Respondent files Adjudication Response within 10 working days of the Adjudication Claim. Must include: all facts, documents, and legal arguments resisting the claim, any set-off or cross-claim. Failure to respond — adjudicator may proceed on the Claimant's materials.
steps.timeframe: Within 10 working days of Adjudication Claim

steps.title: Adjudication Decision (s.12)
steps.description: Adjudicator makes a decision within 45 working days from the Response (extendable if parties agree). The decision is in writing with reasons. If claimant succeeds: respondent must pay the adjudicated amount within the time stipulated. The decision is INTERIM BINDING — an unpaid decision may be enforced as a High Court judgment.

steps.title: Enforcement or Setting Aside
steps.description: Enforcement: If respondent fails to pay, claimant applies to the High Court to enforce the decision as a court judgment (s.28). Setting Aside: Respondent may apply to the High Court to set aside on limited grounds (s.15): fraud, denial of natural justice, lack of independence, excess of jurisdiction. Challenge does NOT automatically stay enforcement.
steps.legalBasis: CIPAA 2012, ss.15, 28; WRP Asia Pacific Sdn Bhd v NS Bluescope [2018] 1 MLJ 1 FC
documents: Summons to Set Aside (s.15) — if applicable

workflows.title: Probate Application — Non-Contentious (Testator with Will)
workflows.description: The procedure for obtaining a Grant of Probate in Malaysia for the estate of a deceased non-Muslim person who left a valid will, from taking instructions through to distribution of the estate.
workflows.legalBasis: Probate and Administration Act 1959 (Act 97); Wills Act 1959 (Act 346); Rules of Court 2012
workflows.applicableTo: Non-Muslim deceased persons who left a valid will — executor applying for Grant of Probate

steps.title: Take Instructions and Obtain Original Will
steps.description: Obtain the original will from the deceased's safe, solicitors who stored it, or the Probate Registry. Confirm: the will is the last and final will, it was duly executed (signed, witnessed), and the executor named is willing and able to act. Take a comprehensive list of all assets and liabilities of the deceased.
documents: Preliminary list of assets and liabilities
steps.timeframe: As soon as possible after death

steps.title: Advertise for Creditors
steps.description: Advertise a Notice to Creditors in a major newspaper (usually one English and one Bahasa Malaysia newspaper) giving creditors 2 months to submit their claims. This protects the executor from personal liability for estate debts if creditors do not come forward.
steps.timeframe: As soon as possible — 2 months run from advertisement date

steps.title: Prepare and File Originating Summons
steps.description: File an Originating Summons (Form 1 PAA 1959) in the High Court Probate Registry of the state where the deceased was domiciled. Accompanied by: original will, certified death certificate, sworn affidavit of executor, Schedule of Assets (full disclosure of all assets and liabilities with estimated values), and Affidavit of scripts.

steps.title: Probate Registry — Requisitions
steps.description: The Probate Registrar examines the application. May raise requisitions (queries) on: will execution, identity of deceased, completeness of Schedule of Assets, or other procedural requirements. Respond to all requisitions promptly.

steps.title: Grant of Probate Issued
steps.description: Once satisfied, the Registrar seals the Grant of Probate. This is the court's official recognition of the executor's authority to administer the estate. The Grant, together with a certified copy of the will, is the executor's authority to deal with all assets of the deceased.

steps.title: Collect and Realise Estate Assets
steps.description: Using the Grant of Probate, the executor collects all assets: presents the Grant to banks to release bank accounts; presents to share registries to transfer shares; presents to EPF, insurance companies, unit trusts. Sell property if necessary or required by will.
steps.legalBasis: PAA 1959; Companies Act 2016 (share transfer); NLC 1965 (land transfer)

steps.title: Pay Debts and Estate Expenses
steps.description: From the estate funds, pay: funeral and testamentary expenses (first priority); secured debts; unsecured debts. Keep detailed accounts. Pay income tax on income earned by the estate after death (executor's liability). Stamp duty on assets transferred (if applicable).
steps.legalBasis: PAA 1959; Income Tax Act 1967; Stamp Act 1949

steps.title: Distribution to Beneficiaries
steps.description: After all debts and expenses are paid, distribute the residuary estate to beneficiaries as directed by the will. Obtain receipts from each beneficiary. Prepare final estate accounts. For property, execute a Memorandum of Assent (Form 14B NLC 1965) to transfer land to beneficiaries.
steps.timeframe: Final distribution after all debts paid

workflows.title: Personal Injury / Motor Accident Claim — Sessions Court
workflows.description: Procedure for commencing a personal injury action arising from a road traffic accident in the Sessions Court (claims ≤ RM1 million) under the Civil Law Act 1956 and Rules of Court 2012.
workflows.legalBasis: Civil Law Act 1956; Road Transport Act 1987, s. 96; Limitation Act 1953, s. 6(1); Public Authorities Protection Act 1948; Subordinate Courts Act 1948
workflows.applicableTo: Plaintiffs injured in road traffic accidents seeking damages from the tortfeasor and/or insurer

steps.title: File Police Report and Obtain Investigation Paper
steps.description: Lodge a police report at the nearest station within 24 hours of the accident. Apply to JSPT (Bahagian Siasatan Trafik) for the Investigation Paper, sketch plan and key statements once investigation is complete.
steps.legalBasis: Road Transport Act 1987; police standing orders
steps.timeframe: Within 24 hours of accident; IP collected 1-3 months later

steps.title: Obtain Medical Reports
steps.description: Obtain medical reports from the treating hospital and follow-up specialists describing injuries, treatment, prognosis, and degree of permanent incapacity (if any). Preserve all medical receipts and bills.
steps.legalBasis: Civil Law Act 1956; rules of evidence
steps.timeframe: As treatment progresses; specialist report typically at 6-12 months post-accident

steps.title: Compute Special and General Damages
steps.description: Itemise special damages (quantifiable past loss): medical expenses, transport, loss of earnings to date. Estimate general damages (PSLA) using the Compendium of Personal Injury Awards (Malaysia). Compute future loss of earnings using multiplier × multiplicand under s. 28A CLA 1956.
steps.legalBasis: Civil Law Act 1956, ss. 7, 28A; Compendium of Personal Injury Awards

steps.title: Send Demand Letter to Tortfeasor and Insurer
steps.description: Issue a formal letter of demand setting out particulars of injury, liability narrative, and quantum. Demand admission of liability and payment within 14 days. Copy to the insurer (s. 96 Road Transport Act 1987 entitles direct action).
steps.legalBasis: Road Transport Act 1987, s. 96; pre-action protocol practice

steps.title: File Writ of Summons and Statement of Claim
steps.description: Prepare and file the Writ + Statement of Claim in the Sessions Court (claims ≤ RM1 million). Plead negligence with full particulars, special and general damages, and pre-judgment interest.
steps.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 6, Order 18; Subordinate Courts Act 1948

steps.title: Serve and Enter Appearance
steps.description: Personally serve the writ on the tortfeasor and insurer. Memorandum of appearance entered within 14 days; defence within 14 days thereafter (O 12, O 18 r 2 ROC 2012).

steps.title: Pre-Trial Case Management and Discovery
steps.description: Comply with pre-trial case management orders. Exchange documents under O 24. Issue interrogatories where appropriate. Obtain medical experts and prepare witness statements.

steps.title: Trial and Judgment
steps.description: Present evidence at trial: plaintiff's testimony on liability and injury, medical experts on prognosis, employer evidence on lost earnings. Cross-examine defence witnesses. Submit closing arguments addressing liability, contributory negligence, and quantum.

workflows.title: Section 20 IRA 1967 — Unfair Dismissal Representation
workflows.description: Procedure for a workman to file a representation under s. 20 Industrial Relations Act 1967 for unfair dismissal, conciliation, and reference to the Industrial Court.
workflows.legalBasis: Industrial Relations Act 1967, ss. 20, 30; Employment Act 1955
workflows.applicableTo: Workmen (as defined under s. 2 IRA 1967) dismissed without just cause or excuse
workflows.estimatedDuration: 12-24 months from filing to Industrial Court award

steps.title: Verify Status as 'Workman' and Time Limit
steps.description: Confirm the claimant falls within the s. 2 IRA 1967 definition of 'workman' (excludes most senior management with broad managerial discretion). Verify the representation is filed within the statutory time limit (60 days from date of dismissal under post-2020 amendment).

steps.title: File Representation with Director General of Industrial Relations
steps.description: Complete and file Form A representation with the Director General at the nearest Department of Industrial Relations office. Set out brief facts of dismissal and prayer for reinstatement (or compensation in lieu).
steps.legalBasis: Industrial Relations Act 1967, s. 20(1); Industrial Relations Regulations

steps.title: Conciliation Meeting
steps.description: Attend conciliation meeting(s) convened by the IR Officer. Both parties present positions and explore settlement. If settlement reached, recorded in a settlement agreement enforceable as Industrial Court award.

steps.title: Reference to Industrial Court
steps.description: If conciliation fails, the case is referred directly to the Industrial Court (post-2020 amendment removed Ministerial reference requirement). The Court issues a notice of mention.
documents: Notice of Mention from Industrial Court

steps.title: File Statement of Case and Statement in Reply
steps.description: Claimant files Statement of Case (akin to Statement of Claim). Employer files Statement in Reply (akin to Defence). Both must comply with Industrial Court Rules 1967.

steps.title: Hearing — Liability Phase
steps.description: Industrial Court conducts hearing. Employer bears the burden to prove (i) misconduct or other ground; (ii) due inquiry; (iii) proportionality of dismissal. Workman gives evidence on dismissal narrative and post-dismissal earnings.
steps.legalBasis: Industrial Relations Act 1967, s. 30(5); Goon Kwee Phoy v J&P Coats

steps.title: Award
steps.description: Industrial Court hands down written Award. If dismissal not for just cause/excuse: reinstatement OR back-wages (capped at 24 months under post-2020 amendment, but see deserving cases) + compensation in lieu (1 month per year of service).
steps.legalBasis: Industrial Relations Act 1967, s. 30; Industrial Relations (Amendment) Act 2020
steps.timeframe: Within 6 months of conclusion of hearing

steps.title: Judicial Review (Optional)
steps.description: Aggrieved party may apply for judicial review under Order 53 ROC 2012 to the High Court within 3 months of the Award. Grounds: illegality, procedural impropriety, irrationality. Filed by Originating Summons + Affidavit + Statement under O 53 r 3.
steps.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 53; R Rama Chandran v Industrial Court [1997] 1 MLJ 145

workflows.title: Order 53 Judicial Review Application
workflows.description: Two-stage procedure for judicial review of public body decisions under Order 53 ROC 2012: leave stage and substantive hearing.
workflows.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 53; Courts of Judicature Act 1964, Schedule, paragraph 1
workflows.applicableTo: Persons adversely affected by decisions of public bodies acting in exercise of public functions
workflows.estimatedDuration: 9-18 months from leave application to substantive determination

steps.title: Identify Decision and Verify Time Limit
steps.description: Identify with precision the impugned decision (date, decision-maker, content). Verify application is made within 3 months from when the grounds first arose under O 53 r 3(6). Consider whether internal/statutory remedies must be exhausted first.

steps.title: Prepare Notice of Application for Leave (Form 109)
steps.description: Draft Notice of Application for Leave; Statement under O 53 r 3 setting out (a) name and description of applicant; (b) relief sought; (c) grounds; and (d) facts relied on. Supporting Affidavit exhibiting the decision and material before decision-maker.

steps.title: File Leave Application Ex Parte
steps.description: File the leave application ex parte at the High Court Registry. Service on the Attorney General is mandatory under O 53 r 3(3). Pay filing fees.

steps.title: Leave Hearing
steps.description: Court hears leave application (now usually inter partes after Service on AG). Test: applicant must show (a) sufficient interest (locus standi); (b) arguable case. Court grants or refuses leave.
steps.legalBasis: Rules of Court 2012, Order 53; case law (Ahmad Jefri Mohd Jahri v Pengarah Kebudayaan Negeri Pahang)

steps.title: Serve Notice of Motion (Form 110)
steps.description: Within 14 days of leave being granted, serve Notice of Motion on the respondents. Substantive affidavits exchanged thereafter; cause papers prepared for hearing.

steps.title: Affidavit Exchange and Cause Papers
steps.description: Respondents file Affidavit in Reply explaining the decision and process. Applicant may file Reply Affidavit. Submit Bundle of Documents and Bundle of Authorities for hearing.

steps.title: Substantive Hearing
steps.description: Court hears substantive judicial review on grounds of illegality, procedural impropriety, irrationality, and (in fundamental rights cases) proportionality. Parties present oral submissions and respond to court's questions.
steps.legalBasis: GCHQ case; Wednesbury; Sivarasa Rasiah v Badan Peguam Malaysia

steps.title: Judgment and Remedies
steps.description: Court delivers judgment. Available remedies: certiorari (quash), prohibition, mandamus, declaration, injunction. Under R Rama Chandran, court may substitute its own decision in proper cases. Costs follow event.
steps.legalBasis: Courts of Judicature Act 1964, Schedule paragraph 1; R Rama Chandran [1997] 1 MLJ 145
steps.timeframe: Within 6 months of conclusion of hearing

workflows.title: Single-Petition Divorce under s. 53 LRA 1976
workflows.description: Procedure for filing a single petition for divorce by one spouse on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage under the Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976.
workflows.legalBasis: Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976, ss. 50, 53, 54, 61; Divorce and Matrimonial Proceedings Rules 1980
workflows.applicableTo: Non-Muslim petitioner whose marriage is registered for at least 2 years (subject to s. 50 exceptions)
workflows.estimatedDuration: 9-18 months from petition to decree absolute

steps.title: Verify Eligibility and Marriage Tribunal
steps.description: Confirm marriage is registered for at least 2 years under s. 50 LRA 1976 (or s. 50 exception applies — exceptional hardship/depravity). Apply to the Marriage Tribunal under s. 106 unless an exception applies (conversion to Islam by spouse, imprisonment 5+ years, mental incapacity).

steps.title: Prepare Petition and Statement of Particulars
steps.description: Draft Petition setting out marriage, children, ground of irretrievable breakdown supported by one of the four facts under s. 54 (adultery, unreasonable behaviour, 2-year desertion, 2-year separation). Statement of Particulars in matrimonial proceedings includes assets, income, custody arrangements.

steps.title: File Petition in High Court
steps.description: File the Petition with marriage certificate, certificate of completion of Marriage Tribunal process (or exemption), filing fee. Issued and sealed.

steps.title: Serve Petition on Respondent
steps.description: Personally serve the Petition on the respondent spouse, with Acknowledgment of Service form. Substituted service requires court order.
documents: Acknowledgment of Service signed by respondent

steps.title: Filing of Answer (if defended)
steps.description: Respondent has 8 days from acknowledgment of service to file an Answer. If undefended, petition proceeds to hearing on the petitioner's evidence.

steps.title: Hearing for Decree Nisi
steps.description: Court hears petition. Petitioner gives oral evidence on marriage, breakdown and supporting fact. Court grants Decree Nisi if satisfied. Ancillary orders on custody, maintenance, and division of matrimonial assets may be made.

steps.title: Apply for Decree Absolute
steps.description: After 3 months from Decree Nisi (s. 61(2) LRA 1976), petitioner applies for Decree Absolute. Application by Notice of Motion + supporting affidavit. Marriage dissolved only on Decree Absolute.
documents: Notice of Motion for Decree Absolute

workflows.title: Section 346 Oppression Action — Companies Act 2016
workflows.description: Procedure for a member to commence proceedings under s. 346 Companies Act 2016 for relief from oppressive or unfairly prejudicial conduct of company affairs.
workflows.legalBasis: Companies Act 2016, s. 346; Rules of Court 2012
workflows.applicableTo: Members, debenture holders, personal representatives of deceased members of a company

steps.title: Compile Evidence of Oppressive Conduct
steps.description: Gather contemporaneous documents evidencing the oppressive conduct: board minutes, resolutions, financial statements, related-party transactions, correspondence. Verify continuing nature of the conduct (s. 346 looks at conduct of affairs).

steps.title: Issue Letter Before Action
steps.description: Send a formal letter to the company and offending parties identifying the oppressive conduct, demanding cessation and (if appropriate) buy-out at fair value. Open settlement window.

steps.title: Prepare Originating Summons and Affidavit
steps.description: Draft Originating Summons setting out the relief sought (commonly buy-out at fair value, regulation of affairs, restraining orders). Affidavit in Support exhibiting all evidence and pleading the oppressive conduct in detail.
steps.legalBasis: Companies Act 2016, s. 346(2); Rules of Court 2012, Order 7

steps.title: Consider Interim Relief
steps.description: Where assets are at risk of dissipation, file Mareva injunction + asset disclosure. Where ongoing oppression continues, seek interim mandatory injunction restoring status quo.
steps.legalBasis: Specific Relief Act 1950, ss. 50-55; inherent jurisdiction

steps.title: File and Serve OS
steps.description: File OS in High Court. Serve on the company and all offending parties (typically directors and other shareholders). Defendants must enter appearance and file Affidavit in Reply.

steps.title: Affidavit Exchange and Discovery
steps.description: Defendants file Affidavit in Reply. Petitioner files Reply Affidavit. Discovery may be ordered for company records, financials, related-party transactions. Cross-examination on affidavits where credibility is in issue.

steps.title: Trial and Valuation
steps.description: Substantive hearing. Where buy-out is sought, court may direct independent valuation by Court-appointed valuer (or accept party valuations). Evidence on fair value as at agreed valuation date.
steps.legalBasis: Companies Act 2016, s. 346(2); Pang Yong Hock v PKM Industries

steps.title: Judgment and Buy-Out Order
steps.description: Court delivers judgment. Common remedy: buy-out at fair value (with directions on valuation, payment terms, share transfer). Other remedies: regulation of affairs, restraint orders, derivative direction, winding up (last resort).
steps.timeframe: Within 6 months of conclusion of hearing

workflows.title: CIPAA 2012 Adjudication
workflows.description: Statutory adjudication procedure under the Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012 for prompt payment dispute resolution in construction contracts.
workflows.legalBasis: Construction Industry Payment and Adjudication Act 2012 (Act 746); CIPAA Regulations 2014
workflows.applicableTo: Parties to written construction contracts within s. 4 CIPAA (work and services in Malaysia)
workflows.estimatedDuration: 10-14 weeks from Payment Claim to Adjudication Decision

steps.title: Serve Payment Claim (s. 5)
steps.description: Unpaid party serves a Payment Claim on the non-paying party. Must include amount claimed, due date, description of work, basis of claim, contract reference. Strict compliance — defective claims are void.

steps.title: Receive Payment Response (s. 6)
steps.description: Non-paying party has 10 working days to serve a Payment Response: admitting in whole or in part, or disputing. Failure to respond is deemed dispute of the entire claim.
steps.timeframe: 10 working days from receipt of Payment Claim

steps.title: Serve Notice of Adjudication (s. 7)
steps.description: If Payment Response is unsatisfactory or absent, claimant serves Notice of Adjudication setting out the dispute, parties, contract reference, amount, and the relief sought.
steps.timeframe: Any time after Payment Response (or default)

steps.title: Appointment of Adjudicator
steps.description: Parties may agree on an adjudicator. Failing agreement within 10 working days, application to KLRCA/AIAC Director for appointment. Adjudicator must be independent and qualified.
steps.timeframe: Within 10 working days of Notice of Adjudication

steps.title: Adjudication Claim
steps.description: Claimant serves Adjudication Claim within 10 working days of adjudicator acceptance. Sets out claim in detail with all documents and submissions.

steps.title: Adjudication Response and Reply
steps.description: Respondent serves Adjudication Response within 10 working days of receiving Claim. Claimant may serve Adjudication Reply within 5 working days of Response. Each party may submit further pleadings only with adjudicator's leave.

steps.title: Adjudication Decision (s. 12)
steps.description: Adjudicator delivers Decision within 45 working days from service of Adjudication Response, extendable by mutual agreement. Decision must be in writing with reasons. Binding until set aside under s. 15 or finally determined by court/arbitration.

steps.title: Enforcement or Setting Aside
steps.description: Successful party enforces under s. 28 (court order to enforce as judgment). Aggrieved party may apply under s. 15 to set aside (fraud, denial of natural justice, lack of independence, excess of jurisdiction). Suspension of work permitted under s. 29 if not paid.
steps.timeframe: Enforcement: any time after non-payment of Decision

workflows.title: Defamation Action — Writ + Statement of Claim
workflows.description: Procedure for commencing a defamation action (libel or slander) under the Defamation Act 1957 and common law in the High Court.
workflows.legalBasis: Defamation Act 1957; Limitation Act 1953, s. 6; Rules of Court 2012
workflows.applicableTo: Persons whose reputation has been damaged by defamatory statements

steps.title: Identify Defamatory Statement
steps.description: Identify the precise defamatory statement (words, where published, when, by whom, to whom). Preserve copies (screenshots for online; physical copies for print). Verify identification of the plaintiff (express or by innuendo).
documents: Original publication or screenshot with metadata

steps.title: Send Concerns Notice / Demand for Apology
steps.description: Send a formal letter identifying the defamatory statement, demanding immediate retraction and apology in equally prominent form, and threatening proceedings if not complied with.

steps.title: Prepare Statement of Claim
steps.description: Draft Statement of Claim identifying: (i) words complained of (verbatim) — extract and exhibit; (ii) natural and ordinary meaning; (iii) any innuendo with extrinsic facts; (iv) publication; (v) reference to plaintiff; (vi) damage. Plead malice (if seeking aggravated damages).
steps.legalBasis: Defamation Act 1957; Rules of Court 2012, Order 18 r 12

steps.title: File Writ in High Court
steps.description: File Writ + Statement of Claim in the High Court (defamation is unliquidated; quantum often substantial). Pay filing fees.

steps.title: Serve and Enter Appearance
steps.description: Personally serve the writ on the defendant (and any joint publishers). Defendant enters appearance within 14 days; defence within 14 days thereafter.

steps.title: Defence — Plead Defences Specifically
steps.description: Defendant must plead defences specifically: justification (with particulars of truth); fair comment (matter of public interest, opinion based on facts); privilege (absolute or qualified); Reynolds defence (responsible journalism). Bare denials inadequate.
steps.legalBasis: Defamation Act 1957, ss. 8, 9; Reynolds v Times Newspapers
documents: Defence with full particulars of defences

steps.title: Discovery, Interrogatories and PTCM
steps.description: Discovery of relevant documents (publication metadata, drafts, instructions to publishers). Interrogatories to identify sources (subject to journalistic privilege). Pre-trial case management orders.

steps.title: Trial and Judgment
steps.description: Trial on liability and quantum. Plaintiff proves publication, defamatory meaning, identification. Defendant proves any positive defence. Quantum: general damages presumed in libel/slander per se; aggravated where conduct of defendant aggravates injury; rare exemplary damages. Court may order injunction restraining further publication.
steps.legalBasis: Defamation Act 1957; Rookes v Barnard; case law on quantum

legal_forms.title: Charge
legal_forms.authorizedBy: National Land Code 1965, s. 243
legal_forms.purpose: To create a registered charge over land as security for a loan or financing facility
legal_forms.instructions: Must be executed by the chargor before a solicitor or a Registrar of Titles. Stamp duty (0.5% of loan amount) payable before presentation to the Land Registry. Two witnesses required. The form must specify the amount secured and the loan agreement details.
legal_forms.filingFee: RM50 registration fee + 0.5% stamp duty on loan amount
legal_forms.timeLimit: Within 3 months of execution (stamp duty), within 6 months (registration)
legal_forms.notes: For Islamic banking: an Islamic Charge (Gadaian Islam) is used for Islamic financing facilities

legal_forms.title: Notice Before Foreclosure (Notice of Default)
legal_forms.authorizedBy: National Land Code 1965, s. 254
legal_forms.purpose: To give the chargor formal notice of default and demand payment of the outstanding amount before commencing foreclosure proceedings
legal_forms.instructions: Must specify the amount outstanding as at the date of the notice and give the chargor a minimum of one month to remedy the default. Served by personal service or registered post. Keep proof of service (acknowledgment receipt or statutory declaration).
fields: Date by which Payment Must be Made
legal_forms.filingFee: No court fee — private notice
legal_forms.timeLimit: Must give at least 1 month from date of notice before Form 16D can be served
legal_forms.notes: Non-service or defective service of Form 16C may render subsequent foreclosure proceedings invalid

legal_forms.title: Notice of Application for Order for Sale
legal_forms.authorizedBy: National Land Code 1965, s. 254; Order 83 ROC 2012
legal_forms.purpose: Formal notice to the chargor of the chargee's intention to apply to the High Court for an Order for Sale
legal_forms.instructions: Served at least one month before the Originating Summons is filed. Must be served after Form 16C and after the chargor has failed to remedy the default. Contents must mirror the requirements of s. 254 NLC.
fields: Total Amount Due (as at date of notice)
Name and Address of Chargee's Solicitors
legal_forms.filingFee: No court fee — private notice
legal_forms.timeLimit: At least 1 month before filing Originating Summons in court

legal_forms.title: Bank Guarantee
legal_forms.authorizedBy: Financial Services Act 2013
legal_forms.purpose: Standard form bank guarantee issued by a bank on behalf of its customer to guarantee performance or payment obligations
legal_forms.instructions: Must clearly state: the principal debtor, the beneficiary, the guaranteed amount, the expiry date, and the governing law. Bank guarantees are demand instruments — payable upon written demand. Legal advice should be obtained on the terms before issuance.
legal_forms.filingFee: Bank commission: typically 0.5% to 2% p.a. of guaranteed amount
legal_forms.timeLimit: Valid until expiry date stated in the guarantee
